_comment: Golden cases for the foreign-issuer classifier (Tool 1).
EVERY CASE BELOW IS PROVISIONAL: verified_by is null, meaning nobody at the bank has
signed the codes off yet. They exist to exercise the machinery and to encode the traps
we expect, NOT to prove accuracy. Scoring reports verified and provisional separately,
and no accuracy figure may be quoted from provisional cases.
To verify a case: have MO confirm both codes, then fill in verified_by and verified_on.
Issuer names are fictional on purpose - a golden case should not assert a classification
about a real company until someone at the bank stands behind it.

cases.description: Special purpose funding vehicle of the Nordkap banking group. Issues bonds on international markets and on-lends the proceeds exclusively to its parent bank and that bank's subsidiaries. Does not take deposits from the public and holds no banking licence of its own.
cases.note: The core trap: the group name contains 'Bank' and the entity issues bank-like paper, but it is a captive finance vehicle, not a bank. Distinguishing 2002703 from 2002213 is the whole point of the ESA half.

cases.description: Účelová finanční společnost skupiny Nordkap Bank. Vydává dluhopisy na mezinárodních trzích a získané prostředky půjčuje výhradně mateřské bance a jejím dceřiným společnostem. Nepřijímá vklady od veřejnosti a nemá vlastní bankovní licenci.
cases.note: Same case in Czech. Pairs with captive-funding-spv to measure how much the pre-filter loses when the description is not in the codebook's language.

cases.description: German manufacturer of passenger cars and light commercial vehicles, operating three assembly plants. Majority owned by a foreign automotive group. Issues bonds to finance its own operations.
cases.note: No financial vocabulary at all. Exists because an early version of the pre-filter returned zero ESA candidates here: the residual sector 'Nefinanční podniky' has to be reachable without a keyword hit.

cases.description: Italian commercial bank licensed by the Bank of Italy, taking retail and corporate deposits and providing loans. Wholly owned by a French banking group.
cases.note: The straightforward bank, and the control axis: foreign-owned, so 2002213 rather than 2002212.

cases.description: Swiss non-life insurance undertaking writing property and casualty business, subsidiary of a foreign insurance group.
cases.note: NACE 65 covers insurance and pension funding together; ESA separates insurers from pension funds.

cases.description: Irish designated activity company established to acquire a portfolio of residential mortgage loans and fund the purchase by issuing rated asset-backed notes. No employees and no activity beyond holding the portfolio.
cases.note: Must land on the securitisation sector 2002513 rather than the generic captive 2002703 - both are 'special purpose' entities in ordinary language.

cases.description: Provides finance leases and instalment credit for commercial vehicles and machinery to business customers. Funded by bank facilities and bond issues. Subsidiary of a foreign industrial group.
cases.note: Lender rather than captive: it lends to third parties, not only within its group.

cases.description: Luxembourg open-ended investment company investing in listed European equities on behalf of institutional investors. Not a money market fund.
cases.note: Explicitly not a money market fund, so 2002403 rather than 2002303.

cases.description: Multilateral development bank owned by member states, financing infrastructure projects in its member countries. Enjoys preferred creditor status and is exempt from national banking supervision.
cases.note: A supranational is neither a resident nor an ordinary foreign bank; it has its own ESA sector. A pre-filter that only knows the word 'bank' will get this wrong.

cases.description: Operates a chain of supermarkets and convenience stores across several European countries. Listed on Euronext.
cases.note: A second non-financial issuer, with the word 'Holdings' in the name to check that it does not drag the answer towards a holding-company classification.
